source.title: CNSSI No. 1253, Categorization and Control Selection for National Security Systems
source.appendix: Appendix D, Tables D-1 through D-20 (PDF pp. 25-161 / D-4 onward)

legend.ref: Appendix D introduction, pp. D-1 to D-2 (PDF pp. 22-23)
legend.X: Identifies applicability of NIST SP 800-53B baselines for NSS.
legend.+: Identifies a control needed to protect NSS and therefore added to the NSS baselines.
legend.--: Identifies a control selected for NIST baseline (security or privacy) but not selected for an NSS baseline (security or privacy). Privacy controls selected for a NIST baseline but not selected for an NSS baseline are specific to systems that process PII and are addressed in the Privacy Overlay. Any control can still be selected during tailoring if needed.
legend.blank: A control not selected for a baseline nor allocated to a particular security objective; no parameter value specific to NSS is provided for the control; or the control is not applicable to an Assurance, Resiliency, or ATT&CK mapping. If not indicated with an "X" or "+", the control may still be selected during the tailoring process.
legend.√: Identifies applicability of a control to Privacy Implementation Considerations, Assurance, Resiliency, or ATT&CK.
legend.privacy_control_baseline: Controls indicated with an "X" or a "+" in this column are required for all NSS.
legend.security_control_baselines: Columns showing the association of a control to the security objective (confidentiality, integrity, availability) and at what impact level (low, moderate, high) based on inclusion of an "X" or a "+".

privacy_implementation_considerations.1: Close coordination between security and privacy is needed to manage privacy risks
privacy_implementation_considerations.2: Design choices may mitigate privacy risks
privacy_implementation_considerations.3: Implementation choices may create unintended privacy risks
privacy_implementation_considerations.4: PII should not flow through or into a system that is not authorized to process PII

legend.parameter_value: Contains minimum values specified for NSS; parameter values not appropriate for CNSS to define for all NSS are not included. Parameter values apply to both privacy and security baselines.
legend.withdrawn: Controls that are designated as "Withdrawn" indicate they are no longer in the NIST SP 800-53 control catalog.

selection_rule.ref: Section 3.2.1, Task S-1, Control Selection, p. 10 (PDF p. 14); trigraph per Section 3.1.2, p. 10 (PDF p. 14)
text: 1. Select the NSS security control baseline contained in Appendix D Tables D-1 through D-20 corresponding to the security categorization of the system (i.e., the impact levels determined for each security objective [confidentiality, integrity, and availability]).
2. Include the NSS privacy control baseline contained in Appendix D Tables D-1 through D-20, which is a default for all NSS.
selection_rule.trigraph: For each security objective, determine the overall high water mark for information types on the system ... This results in three distinct high water marks, one for each security objective ... shown as a trigraph categorization (e.g., L-L-L, M-M-H).
selection_rule.implemented_as: baseline = {rows marked X or + in the C column at the system's C level} ∪ {… I column at the I level} ∪ {… A column at the A level} ∪ {rows marked X or + in the Privacy Control Baseline column}; withdrawn rows and '--' / blank cells are never selected. No overall (single) high-water mark is used for NSS selection.

Table D-13.note: Deployed organization-wide. Supports information security program. Not associated with security control baselines. Independent of any system impact level.

Table D-15.note: Personally Identifiable Information Processing and Transparency control are not allocated to the security control baselines.
